name: Merlin-class Engine
description: A reliable medium-thrust engine. Good balance of thrust and efficiency for most missions.

params.label: Engine Count
params.explain: More engines = more thrust and redundancy, but heavier and more expensive. Wear multiplied by count.

params.label: Thrust Scale
params.explain: Scales thrust and fuel flow. Higher thrust improves TWR but burns fuel faster.

params.label: Efficiency (Isp)
params.explain: Higher efficiency = more Δv from same fuel. But high-efficiency engines usually have lower thrust.

params.label: Gimbal Range
params.explain: Wider gimbal gives better steering during powered flight. Adds complexity and slight wear.

name: Draco-class Engine
description: A small, high-efficiency engine. Excellent for low-gravity bodies and precision manoeuvres.

params.label: Engine Count
params.explain: More Draco engines increase thrust and redundancy at low individual weight.

params.label: Thrust Scale
params.explain: Scales thrust output. Draco engines are low-thrust by design — best for precision, not hovering on heavy planets.

params.label: Efficiency (Isp)
params.explain: High base efficiency makes these engines fuel-efficient. Slight scaling room.

params.label: Gimbal Range
params.explain: Limited gimbal; RCS handles most attitude control for this engine class.

name: Standard Propellant Tank
description: A cylindrical aluminium propellant tank. Reliable workhorse for most missions.

params.label: Tank Volume
params.explain: Larger volume = more fuel = more Δv, but heavier dry mass and higher cost. The rocket equation makes this non-linear.

params.label: Pressurised
params.explain: Pressurised tanks feed engines more reliably at high altitude. Adds mass and cost.

name: Lightweight Composite Tank
description: Carbon-composite tank. Lower dry mass penalty but costs more and wears faster.

params.label: Tank Volume
params.explain: Same fuel at lower structural mass. Great for Δv-limited missions.

name: RCS Thruster Block
description: Cold-gas attitude control thrusters. Handles fine manoeuvring and tilt correction.

params.label: Thruster Count
params.explain: More RCS thrusters = better attitude control and corrections, but adds mass and fuel use.

params.label: Thruster Strength
params.explain: Stronger RCS snaps to orientation faster. Important on windy or rotating descent.

name: Standard Landing Leg
description: Four-leg aluminium landing system. Decent stability, moderate mass.

params.label: Leg Count
params.explain: 4 legs are more stable than 3. 3 legs save mass. Both meet the minimum.

params.label: Leg Length
params.explain: Longer legs allow landing on rougher terrain and tolerate more tilt. Heavier.

params.label: Footpad Width
params.explain: Wider footpads spread load over soft regolith. Wider = less sinking risk.

params.label: Shock Absorber
params.explain: Stiffer absorbers tolerate harder touchdowns but transmit more force to the hull on rough landings.

name: Wide-Stance Landing Leg
description: Wider, heavier legs for slope tolerance and rough terrain. Used on Mars and Titan missions.

params.label: Leg Count
params.explain: More legs for more stability on soft or uneven ground.

params.label: Leg Length
params.explain: Wide-stance legs are already long; extending further improves slope tolerance.

params.label: Shock Absorber
params.explain: High shock absorption lets you land harder without damaging the hull or instruments.

name: Standard Spacecraft Bus
description: A basic aluminium spacecraft structure. Reliable and cheap.

params.label: Bus Size
params.explain: Larger bus provides more mounting points and structural strength, but adds mass.

params.label: Material Grade
params.explain: Higher grade = stronger, lighter, pricier alloy. Grade 3 is aerospace titanium.

name: Solar Panel Array
description: Deployable solar panels. Light and free energy — but output depends on distance from the Sun.

params.label: Panel Area
params.explain: More area = more power generated. Power scales with area and solar flux of the target body.

params.label: Cell Efficiency
params.explain: Higher-efficiency cells cost more but generate more power per unit area.

name: Battery Pack
description: Lithium-ion battery pack. Stores power for night-side or shadow operations.

params.label: Battery Capacity
params.explain: More capacity = longer survival in shadow. Heavy. Needed on Titan (low solar flux) or for long nights.

params.label: Cell Banks
params.explain: Multiple banks provide redundancy — one failure leaves others intact.

name: Low-Gain Antenna
description: Omnidirectional antenna. Low data rate but always pointed at Earth.

params.label: Antenna Size
params.explain: Larger antenna = more signal gain = higher data rate. Mass and cost scale with size.

name: High-Gain Dish Antenna
description: Directional dish antenna. High data rate for science-heavy missions. Must be pointed at Earth.

params.label: Dish Size
params.explain: Larger dish = higher data rate. Critical for missions with high science data volume.

params.label: Tracking Speed
params.explain: Faster tracking keeps the dish pointed at Earth through the mission. Faster = more power.

name: Basic Flight Computer
description: Entry-level flight computer. Provides basic stabilisation. No fancy autopilot.

params.label: Computer Tier
params.explain: Tier 1 = basic stabilisation. Tier 2 = autonomous correction. Tier 3 = full autopilot assist. Higher tier = more power and cost.

name: Wide-Angle Camera
description: Visible-light imager. Captures surface geology and landing area images.

params.label: Resolution
params.explain: Higher resolution = better science images but more data per photo. Balance with antenna capacity.

name: Mass Spectrometer
description: Identifies chemical composition of atmosphere and surface samples. Required for mineral surveys.

params.label: Sensitivity
params.explain: Higher sensitivity detects trace compounds. Required to identify perchlorate salts or organic molecules.

name: Percussive Drill
description: Extracts subsurface samples. Required to find subsurface ice and buried minerals.

params.label: Max Drill Depth
params.explain: Deeper drill reaches richer subsurface samples. Heavier mechanism, more power, faster wear.

name: Broadband Seismometer
description: Measures ground vibrations. Required for interior structure mapping missions. Must be deployed gently.

params.label: Frequency Range
params.explain: Wider frequency range captures more types of seismic events. More data, more science value.

name: Ablative Heat Shield
description: PICA-style ablative heat shield. Single-use. Required for entry into thick atmospheres.

params.label: Shield Size
params.explain: Larger shield handles hotter entries (Venus, fast Mars entry). Heavier.

params.label: Ablator Thickness
params.explain: Thicker ablator survives more heating. Required for Venus. Adds mass.

name: Supersonic Parachute
description: Disk-gap-band parachute. Single-use. Effective in Mars and Titan atmospheres.

params.label: Parachute Diameter
params.explain: Larger parachute creates more drag, slows descent more. Very effective on Titan's thick atmosphere. Single-use.
